messages.content:
These are all normal distal nephron and collecting duct epithelium: thick ascending limb (TAL; clusters 10 and 23), connecting tubule and principal cells (clusters 14 and 12), and intercalated cells (clusters 26 and 18). Proximal (LRP2, CUBN), injury (HAVCR1, VCAM1) and urothelial (UPK1B, KRT5) markers are essentially absent.

Evidence:
- TAL, cluster 10 (high confidence): SLC12A1 (0.83 of cells), UMOD (0.57), CASR (0.67) and KCNJ1 (0.78) [Fig 1A](view:1A).
- TAL, cluster 23 (medium): SLC12A1 (0.71) and UMOD (0.76), plus higher CLDN16 (0.51), KNG1, SERPINA5 and NOS1 (0.34). This may be a cortical TAL state that includes some macula densa cells. Its SLC12A3 (0.34) and TRPM6 hint at early distal convoluted tubule cells mixed in.
- Principal cells, cluster 12 (high): AQP2 (0.83), SCNN1G (0.72), AQP3, GATA3 and HSD11B2 [Fig 1B](view:1B).
- Connecting tubule, cluster 14 (medium): the same principal-cell program plus CALB1 (0.84, versus 0.69 in cluster 12) and some TRPM6.
- Intercalated cells, clusters 26 and 18: FOXI1, ATP6V1B1, ATP6V0D2 and HEPACAM2 [Fig 1C](view:1C).
  - Cluster 26 (high) is the purest. It mixes type A (SLC4A1, 0.61) and type B (SLC26A4, 0.43) cells, so subtype confidence is low.
  - Cluster 18 (medium) also carries AQP2 (0.67) and SCNN1G (0.44). This could be connecting-tubule intercalated cells, or principal-cell spillover.

Check whether cluster 18's AQP2 signal comes from cells next to principal cells (spillover) rather than intrinsic expression?

messages.content:
Not settled yet, but the pure intercalated cluster 26 also detects AQP2 in 72% of cells. So cluster 18's principal-cell signal (AQP2 0.67, SCNN1G 0.44, AQP3 0.36) is only modestly above what every intercalated cluster picks up. That fits transcripts spilling over between tightly packed collecting-duct cells more than a distinct cell type [Fig 2A](view:2A).

Settling it needs a per-cell neighborhood test, which I've drafted. It asks whether AQP2 detection in clusters 18 and 26 rises with the number of adjacent principal or connecting-tubule cells (clusters 12 and 14), and whether cluster 18's excess disappears once neighbors are accounted for.

Evidence:
- Cluster 26 versus cluster 18: AQP2 0.72 vs 0.67, SCNN1G 0.28 vs 0.44, AQP3 0.31 vs 0.36.
- Cluster 18 keeps a clear intercalated-cell identity: FOXI1 0.77, SLC4A1 0.68, NHERF1 0.69.

messages.content:
Yes, all three are endothelial cells (high confidence), and the markers point to three different vascular beds: peritubular capillary (cluster 13), glomerular capillary (cluster 20) and arteriolar (cluster 25). Their modest VWF fits this, since VWF is high mainly in large vessels and low in capillaries.

Evidence:
- Shared endothelial program in all three: PECAM1 (0.87–1.00 of cells), PTPRB, EGFL7, KDR, TEK and EPAS1. Enrichr's top hit is endothelial in both libraries for each cluster ([13](https://maayanlab.cloud/Enrichr/enrich?dataset=9d31a8f62f77ba7a7b449403e3004166), [20](https://maayanlab.cloud/Enrichr/enrich?dataset=8b787063dbedc975b601205611c234bf), [25](https://maayanlab.cloud/Enrichr/enrich?dataset=f31a1e74e1b1f62c28393722ea489cb7)).
- Cluster 13, peritubular capillary (medium): PLVAP (0.52), DNASE1L3, RAMP3 and SLCO2A1, which fit fenestrated peritubular capillaries [Fig 1A](view:1A).
- Cluster 20, glomerular capillary (medium): EMCN (0.96), PODXL (0.87), CLIC5 (0.81), IL1RL1 and BTNL9. Its cells form the round clusters scattered through the cortex, which look like glomeruli [Fig 1B](view:1B). PODXL and CLIC5 are also podocyte genes, so some podocyte spillover is possible.
- Cluster 25, arteriolar (medium-low): SEMA3G (0.88), CDH5, CLEC14A, ID1 and TM4SF1. SEMA3G marks afferent and efferent arteriole endothelium [Fig 1C](view:1C).
- One gap: the values returned for EHD3, GJA5 and NPHS1/NPHS2 did not include these three clusters. So the glomerular and arteriolar subtypes aren't confirmed with those genes, and podocyte contamination of cluster 20 isn't ruled out.

Check EHD3, GJA5 and NPHS2 across clusters 13, 20 and 25 to confirm the subtypes?

messages.content:
Cluster 20 sits with cluster 16 because both are inside the same glomerulus [Fig 1A](view:1A). Cluster 20 is the capillary endothelium and cluster 16 looks like the podocytes wrapped around those capillaries, so their interleaving is normal anatomy. Cluster 16 is the top cluster for NPHS1, NPHS2, WT1, PTPRO, CLIC5 and PODXL, which makes it podocytes rather than a nephron tubule. Labels are applied to clusters 13, 20, 25 and 16.

Evidence:
- The image shows a glomerular tuft inside Bowman's capsule, with clusters 20 and 16 interspersed across the capillary loops and tubules outside it [Fig 1A](view:1A).
- Cluster 20 is glomerular endothelium: EMCN (0.96), KDR (0.90), PECAM1 (0.89) and PLAT. Its PODXL and CLIC5 are shared glomerular-capillary and podocyte genes.
- Cluster 16 is podocytes (medium confidence): the Clustergram ranks it top for NPHS1, NPHS2, WT1 and PTPRO [Fig 1B](view:1B). The value table I received cuts off before clusters 16, 20, 25 and 13, so its per-cluster fractions, and the EHD3/GJA5 check for the endothelial subtypes, aren't visible to me.

Check cluster 16's top 25 markers to confirm podocytes over parietal epithelium?

messages.content:
Confirmed: cluster 16 is podocytes (high confidence), not parietal epithelium. Cluster 5, the other large population in this glomerulus (75 cells in view), looks like mesangial cells.

Evidence:
- Cluster 16 is classic podocyte: NPHS2 (0.92 of cells), NPHS1 (0.88), PTPRO (0.81), PODXL (0.98), CLIC5 and PLA2R1. Enrichr's top hit is podocyte in both libraries ([Enrichr](https://maayanlab.cloud/Enrichr/enrich?dataset=f5e5153c84241546fdd5c793c10b08c7)).
- Parietal epithelial markers CLDN1, PAX8 and KRT8 are not among cluster 16's top 25 markers; CLDN1 instead peaks in cluster 7 (with CFH and some WT1), a candidate for parietal epithelium along Bowman's capsule [Fig 2A](view:2A).
- Cluster 5, mesangial or glomerular stromal (medium): PDGFRB (0.48), ITGA8 (0.21), AGTR1, NOTCH3 and SYNPO. PanglaoDB lists mesangial, juxtaglomerular and pericyte terms in its top hits ([Enrichr](https://maayanlab.cloud/Enrichr/enrich?dataset=c4fa242d53817b5038ccdcd34e326a1e)).
- Cluster 5 also carries EMCN (0.49) and NPHS2 (0.12), likely spillover from the packed tuft. Its C7, PDGFRA and INMT suggest it also contains some interstitial fibroblasts or pericytes.

messages.content:
Probably yes. Podocyte-restricted genes turn up at low levels only in the clusters that sit inside the glomerular tuft, not in endothelium elsewhere, which points to spillover from adjacent podocytes rather than true endothelial expression.

The snapshot I have doesn't include NPHS1's values for cluster 20, so the comparison below uses other podocyte-only genes.

Evidence:
- In glomerular endothelium (cluster 20): WT1 0.16 of cells, ZDHHC6 0.35.
- In peritubular endothelium (cluster 13), the out-of-glomerulus control: WT1 0.00, ZDHHC6 0.13.
- In the other cell types inside or next to the tuft: WT1 is 0.11 in mesangial cluster 5 and 0.12 in cluster 7, a possible parietal-cell cluster.
- In podocytes (cluster 16), the likely source: WT1 0.75, ZDHHC6 0.85, NPHS1 0.88 [Fig 3A](view:3A).
- Not usable as evidence: PODXL (0.87) and SYNPO (0.77) in cluster 20. Glomerular endothelium can express both genuinely, so they don't separate the two explanations.

A per-cell test would settle it: whether NPHS1 and NPHS2 detection in cluster 20 rises with the number of adjacent podocytes, using cluster 13 as a control. Draft that notebook?

cells.source:
Tests whether podocyte genes (NPHS1, NPHS2, WT1) detected in glomerular endothelium (cluster 20)
scale with the number of neighboring podocytes (cluster 16), a signature of segmentation spillover.
Peritubular endothelium (cluster 13) is a control. Paths assume the standard Celldega landscape layout;
adjust if your files differ. Set RADIUS in the data's coordinate units.

import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.formula.api as smf
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree
BASE = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/broadinstitute/Celldega_Atera_v1_WTA_Kidney_non_diseased_FFPE/3a46ab4db67821eef3b8ff8d1c3704fb7b3bb48f"
RADIUS = 15
GENES = ["NPHS1", "NPHS2", "WT1", "EMCN"]
meta = pd.read_parquet(f"{BASE}/cell_metadata.parquet")
clus = pd.read_parquet(f"{BASE}/cell_clusters/cluster.parquet")
print(meta.columns.tolist(), clus.columns.tolist())

xc = [c for c in meta.columns if c.lower() in ("center_x", "x", "x_centroid")][0]
yc = [c for c in meta.columns if c.lower() in ("center_y", "y", "y_centroid")][0]
df = pd.DataFrame({"x": meta[xc], "y": meta[yc]})
df["cluster"] = clus.iloc[:, 0].astype(str).reindex(df.index)
for g in GENES:
    df[g] = pd.read_parquet(f"{BASE}/cbg/{g}.parquet").iloc[:, 0].reindex(df.index).fillna(0)
tree = cKDTree(df.loc[df.cluster == "16", ["x", "y"]].values)
ec = df[df.cluster.isin(["20", "13"])].copy()
ec["n_pod"] = [len(n) for n in tree.query_ball_point(ec[["x", "y"]].values, RADIUS)]
ec["pod_bin"] = pd.cut(ec.n_pod, [-1, 0, 1, 2, 100], labels=["0", "1", "2", "3+"])
for g in GENES:
    ec[f"{g}_pos"] = (ec[g] > 0).astype(int)
ec.to_csv("cluster20_13_podocyte_neighbors.csv")

print("Mean podocyte neighbors:\n", ec.groupby("cluster").n_pod.mean(), "\n")
for g in GENES:
    print(f"{g} detection by cluster x podocyte-neighbor bin:")
    print(ec.groupby(["cluster", "pod_bin"], observed=True)[f"{g}_pos"].mean().unstack().round(2), "\n")
sub = ec[ec.cluster == "20"]
for g in ["NPHS1", "NPHS2"]:
    m = smf.logit(f"{g}_pos ~ n_pod", data=sub).fit(disp=0)
    print(g, "in cluster 20: OR per podocyte neighbor", round(np.exp(m.params["n_pod"]), 2), "p", round(m.pvalues["n_pod"], 4))
